brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb (a centre cell with six around it)
requirements.evidence: 7 full hex bases: the centre one at (0,0) and six around it at (1,0), (1,-1), (0,-1), (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,1). 12 joint bolts lock every shared wall, so there is no LOOSE_BODY warning.

requirements.requirement: Work surface covered on top (every cell has a top cover)
requirements.evidence: There are 7 full top covers, one on each base, making a flush top surface.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: There are 18 solid caps, one on each outside face of the six outer cells (3 per cell). These were all the cap places offered. check_build shows no OPEN_CAP_FACE issue.

finish.summary: Seven-cell honeycomb work surface: 7 full bases in a flower shape, 7 top covers, 18 caps and 12 joint bolts (44 parts). check_build reports no issues and the mesh check is clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
